preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner or an authorized address
Victim user must hold some SHF tokens

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner or authorized address, call the multiTransfer function specifying a victim user's address as the 'from' parameter and your own address as one of the recipients. This will transfer tokens from the victim's balance to your address without requiring their approval, bypassing normal transfer restrictions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has owner-only functions that can drain funds from the contract. Specifically, clearStuckBalance() allows the owner to withdraw any BNB in the contract, and clearStuckToken() allows draining any ERC20 tokens. Since the vulnerability is 'Owner Privilege Abuse', we need to impersonate the owner to call these functions and steal funds.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call clearStuckBalance() to drain all BNB from the contract to our address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the owner address from the contract. 2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner. 3. Call clearStuckBalance(100) to drain 100% of BNB. 4. Verify our BNB balance increased.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract collects SHF tokens as fees (in takeFee() function) and stores them in its own address. The owner can use clearStuckToken() to drain these tokens. Since the vulnerability is economic, we should target the token balance which is likely more valuable.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner and drain all SHF tokens from the contract using clearStuckToken().
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the owner address. 2. Impersonate the owner. 3. Call clearStuckToken(TARGET, 0) - passing 0 means drain all tokens. 4. Verify our SHF token balance increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The contract had minimal BNB balance (1 wei), so clearStuckBalance() didn't give us meaningful profit. We need to target the contract's token balance instead.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The multiTransfer() function is callable by authorized addresses (owner is authorized). It can transfer tokens from any address (including the contract itself) to multiple recipients. We can use it to transfer the contract's SHF tokens directly to our attacker address.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner and use multiTransfer() to transfer all SHF tokens from the contract to our attacker address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the owner address. 2. Check contract's SHF token balance. 3. Prepare arrays for multiTransfer(). 4. Impersonate owner and call multiTransfer() to transfer contract's tokens to our address. 5. Verify we received the tokens.
attempts.failure_reflection: The clearStuckToken() function sends tokens to msg.sender (the owner), not to our attacker address. We need to use multiTransfer() which allows transferring tokens from any address (including the contract) to multiple recipients, and we can specify our address as recipient.
